## The fixed-data bargain

<Term id="offline-reinforcement-learning">Offline RL</Term> learns from a static set of transitions `(observation, action, reward, next observation, termination)` produced by one or more behavior policies <Cite id="offline-rl-tutorial-2020" />. Value learning bootstraps, so error from actions outside the data accumulates through the Bellman backup <Cite id="bear-2019" />. For robots, support also spans controller mode, action magnitude, contact regime and task stage, and Real-ORL, built on over 6,500 trajectories from 800 robot hours, found that offline RL and imitation prefer different action spaces <Cite id="real-orl-2022" />.

<OfflineValueOverreach className="my-6" />

## Audit the dataset before choosing a method

### Behavior coverage

Map each episode's source (expert, novice, scripted controller, older policy or exploration) and its actions by task stage. D4RL builds its datasets from hand-designed controllers, human demonstrators, multitask data and policy mixtures <Cite id="d4rl-2020" />.

### Outcome coverage

The reward must separate successes, partial progress and failures, though a completion label can suffice: COG chained four robot skills under a +1/0 reward, from prior data that never solved the new task <Cite id="cog-2020" />.

### Transition integrity

Check timestamps, episode boundaries, terminations and action units. Mishandled time limits cause state aliasing and invalidate experience replay <Cite id="time-limits-2017" />.

### Deployment overlap

Judge support in the policy's input representation and in physical operating variables, where a camera or control-rate change can outweigh the task label. PTR learned new tasks in a new domain on a real WidowX from as few as 10 demonstrations after offline RL pretraining <Cite id="ptr-2022" />. The [datasets guide](/data-hardware/datasets) and the [robot-learning stack](/data-hardware/robot-learning-stack) cover selection and provenance.

## Four ways to remain close to evidence

Offline-RL methods differ in how they keep improvement away from unsupported values, and Park and colleagues find the policy-extraction step often matters more than the value objective <Cite id="park-bottleneck-2024" />.

### Conservative value estimation

Conservative Q-Learning penalizes high values on actions outside the dataset while preserving observed ones <Cite id="cql-2020" />. RankQ's authors argue that such pessimism anchors policies to suboptimal data, and their action ranking raised a VLA's real cube-stacking success from 43.1% to 88.9% <Cite id="rankq-2026" />.

### Avoiding unseen-action queries

Implicit Q-Learning fits a state value by expectile regression over dataset actions and extracts a policy by advantage weighting, so value fitting never queries a new action <Cite id="iql-2022" />.

### Regularizing the policy toward behavior

TD3+BC adds a cloning term and state normalization to an off-policy actor-critic and matches more elaborate algorithms <Cite id="td3-bc-2021" />.

### Discretizing and scaling the value function

QT-Opt trained a Q-function on over 580,000 real grasp attempts and reached 96% success on unseen objects <Cite id="qt-opt-2018" />. With datasets up to 1000 times the usual size, many offline RL algorithms still saturate well short of maximum performance, and long horizons form a fundamental barrier <Cite id="horizon-reduction-2025" />.

## When behavior cloning is the better tool

Behavior cloning is the default for clean expert demonstrations: it fits the action labels and has no bootstrapped critic. Robomimic found recurrent cloning a strong baseline on human demonstrations, where batch-RL methods struggled <Cite id="robomimic-2021" />, and Kumar and colleagues favor offline RL for sparse rewards, suboptimal or noisy data, and long horizons with composable trajectories <Cite id="offline-rl-vs-bc-2022" />.

<TrajectoryStitching className="my-6" />

Neither method repairs missing support. Over 240 hours of demonstrations and over 3,000 rollouts, Robo-ValueRL ties success to value reliability, and reliable values let offline RL scale better than quality-agnostic cloning <Cite id="robo-valuerl-2026" />. The [behavior-cloning guide](/manipulation/bc-foundations) covers the baseline.

<span id="an-evaluation-protocol-that-does-not-flatter-the-critic" />
## A six-step evaluation protocol

Do not choose checkpoints by the Q-values they maximize. Paine and colleagues found offline RL algorithms not robust to hyperparameters, yet able to rank policies reliably once the algorithm and Q-estimation method are controlled <Cite id="paine-hparam-2020" />.

### 1. Lock the data split by deployment factor

Aljalbout and colleagues' survey covers all four, splitting methods that reduce the gap from those that overcome it .
## Domain randomization: train on a distribution of simulators Jakobi and colleagues found in 1995 that sim-to-real correspondence depended on how much noise the simulation used . Tobin and colleagues randomized textures, lighting and camera pose for tabletop object localization; their best network localized objects to about 1.5 cm over 480 webcam images of eight geometric objects, though most runs used ImageNet initialization (random initialization nearly matched it given enough simulated data), and their abstract frames the real world as "just another variation" once the simulator varies enough . Peng and colleagues randomized link mass, joint damping, friction, controller gains, action timing and observation noise, maximizing expected return over [that dynamics distribution](/how-robots-work/#worlds). A recurrent policy trained only in simulation pushed a puck with a seven-DoF Fetch arm, with start and target positions randomized within a 30 cm square . OpenAI's 2018 hand policy randomized friction coefficients and object appearance and transferred to the physical robot . Its Rubik's-cube successor added a curriculum version, automatic domain randomization, which widens ranges as the policy succeeds . Isaac Lab, the [GPU-parallel training framework](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl), ships ADR as a configurable curriculum, but mass, friction, contact offsets and joint armature change through PhysX CPU APIs. Most parameters randomize at runtime, mesh scale and collider type only before simulation starts . SPI-Active notes that poorly tuned randomization "can lead to overly conservative policies" . ## Teacher-student distillation: privilege in, proprioception out Teacher-student training splits sensing from control: a teacher learns from privileged simulator state, then a student with deployable sensing imitates it. Learning by Cheating used this two-stage form for driving , after asymmetric actor-critic had given only the critic full state . Lee and colleagues distilled a privileged RL teacher, which saw simulator-only terrain and contact information, into a temporal convolutional student via its actions and latent features. The student uses two seconds of proprioceptive history, plus the command and current state, and one controller per robot generation took ANYmal-B and ANYmal-C robots through mud, snow, rubble and vegetation without environment-specific tuning . Isaac Lab's DextrAH-RGB example distills a privileged KUKA and Allegro teacher into a stereo-RGB network , and VIRAL's authors report that scaling to tens of GPUs, up to 64, made teacher and student training reliable for an RGB humanoid that ran up to 54 loco-manipulation cycles . RMA trains a base policy and an environment-factor encoder jointly with RL, then regresses an adaptation module on simulated state-action histories to predict the latent extrinsics. The module reads 50 state-action steps (0.5 seconds) and updates asynchronously at about 10 Hz on the A1, while the base policy runs at 100 Hz on the latest estimate, with no online gradient updates. The paper reports adaptation in fractions of a second without real-world fine-tuning, and failures after large perturbations or multiple leg obstructions; its latent encodes behavior-relevant conditions without guaranteeing each physical parameter . UP-OSI had earlier fed dynamics parameters predicted from recent history into a universal policy . Isaac Lab calls the failure mode an information gap due to input mismatch: the student must reconstruct unobserved states from partial observations such as images, hardest under heavy camera occlusion . The teacher-student panel illustrates this with authored terrain and noise, so its errors rise by construction. ## System identification: measure the gap instead Randomization averages over model error, and system identification measures it. Hwangbo and colleagues fitted an actuator network for ANYmal's series-elastic actuators to real excitation data, predicting torque from joint-position errors and velocities now and 0.01 and 0.02 seconds earlier; policies trained with ideal or analytical actuator models failed to take a single step without falling . Tan and colleagues paired an identified actuator model and simulated latency with randomization . SPI-Active samples parameters in parallel with Fisher-information-driven excitation and beats baselines by 42 to 63% in locomotion tasks , and Miller and colleagues tune Spot simulation against hardware with CMA-ES . ASAP pretrains phase-conditioned tracking policies in IsaacGym on retargeted human motions, runs them on a Unitree G1, and records trajectories with motion capture and onboard sensors. A second PPO policy learns a delta action added before the simulator step, the tracking policy is fine-tuned with the frozen delta model in simulation, and only the tracking policy is deployed. For the hardware study the delta covers only four ankle DoFs of the 23-DoF model . Evaluation separates IsaacGym-to-IsaacSim and IsaacGym-to-Genesis tests, with open-loop replay and closed-loop tracking over 43 motion sequences, and ASAP does not win every metric: in the easy IsaacSim closed-loop group its mean global joint-position error is 106 mm against SysID's 105 mm. On hardware, compared only with Vanilla, the error falls from 61.2 to 50.2 mm on kicking and from 159 to 112 mm on LeBron James's "Silencer" . ASAP reports better tracking on the held-out "Silencer" motion without establishing coverage of arbitrary unseen skills, and its stated hardware limits are motor overheating and damage, motion-capture dependence and the data needed for a full 23-DoF delta model . Swift's champion-level drone racing likewise combined simulation RL with physical-world data . ## Real-to-sim: rebuild the scene, keep the physics SplatSim replaces mesh rendering with Gaussian splats reconstructed from the deployment scene, while PyBullet supplies physics. Across four UR5 tasks with 40 trials each, diffusion policies trained on its simulated demonstrations reached 86.25% zero-shot real success, against 97.5% for real-data policies, with training augmentations included . The setup uses a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper and two RealSense D455 cameras, and splat preparation needs manual robot segmentation, CAD-derived link bounds and ICP alignment. The setup figure lists RGB plus end-effector pose as inputs, while the problem statement says the policy uses only RGB at test time . ZEST trains motion-imitation policies with RL from motion capture, monocular video and animation, and deploys them zero-shot on Atlas, the Unitree G1 and Spot . ## Three decompositions ship in 2026 HOVER distills full-body kinematic motion imitation across control modes into one policy . ResGAC combines geometric admittance feedback with residual RL for precise end-effector tracking during whole-body motion . Figure, NVIDIA and Google DeepMind each shipped whole-body control in 2026 with the learning boundary in a different place. ### A unified motion-tracking policy: Figure Helix 02 S0 Figure announced Helix 02 on 27 January 2026. It keeps the tracking decomposition: S2 reasons over scenes and language and emits latent goals; S1, a 200 Hz visuomotor transformer, maps head and palm cameras, fingertip tactile sensors and full-body proprioception to whole-body joint targets; and S0, a 10M-parameter controller at 1 kHz, turns joint state and base motion into actuator commands. S0 trained on over 1,000 hours of joint-level retargeted human motion and sim-to-real RL across more than 200,000 parallel environments, and the headline demo is a 4-minute dishwasher unload and reload . Figure says it later conditioned S0 on camera perception , and reports that Helix 2.5, pretrained from random initialization on its Index human-behavior dataset, succeeded on 56% of blind zero-shot trials in 30 unseen homes, against 9% when trained from scratch . ### A VLA above a learned controller: GR00T + GEAR-SONIC NVIDIA keeps the VLA and whole-body controller as separate learned systems, and released GR00T N1.7 as early access on 18 April 2026 . GR00T N1.7 is a 3B-parameter VLA with a Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone and a flow-matching action head; with the `UNITREE_G1_SONIC` embodiment it predicts latent action tokens that the GEAR-SONIC controller, running at 50 Hz, decodes into joint commands for legs, arms and hands . SONIC (Science Robotics) scales tracking from 1.2M to 42M parameters on 700 hours of motion capture, with one token space serving VR teleoperation and VLAs . Code is under Apache 2.0 and weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, and every checkpoint loads the gated Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone . Qiayuan Liao, Pieter Abbeel, Koushil Sreenath and colleagues at UC Berkeley (October 2026) train a tracker with analytic gradients through short rollouts of a differentiable world model fit to logged simulator transitions . Their SuperMimic passed the return of the released SONIC checkpoint after 3 hours on one H100 GPU, where SONIC trained for 7 days on 128 L40 GPUs, and failed on 25 of its 129,514 training motions against 179 for SONIC . The authors note that the GPU models differ and that SuperMimic trained on the public part of SONIC's data, about 2.3 times less motion . ### One VLA, feet to fingertips: Gemini Robotics 2 Google DeepMind puts everything in one model: its 30 July 2026 announcement reports that Gemini Robotics 2 controls full humanoids "from feet to fingertips", fetching and shelving a watering can on Apptronik's Apollo 2. One checkpoint runs Apollo 2 with SharpaWave hands, Apollo 2 with Inspire hands and the Franka Duo with Robotiq grippers, and DeepMind reports adapting to new bi-arm robots in a few hours, with fewer than 200 examples in most cases . DeepMind says its robots "have more to advance in movement speed" . ## What tracking does not solve A tracker does not choose its own motion. Workhorse trains a visual planner and whole-body tracker separately on the same human poses, augmenting each for the other's deployment errors . HDMI extracts human and object trajectories from monocular video, then trains policies to track both . Zhang and colleagues pair a terrain-aware diffusion motion generator with a tracker fine-tuned on its imperfect references, crossing boxes, hurdles and stairs on a G1 . VIRAL's simulation-trained RGB policy ran continuous loco-manipulation for up to 54 cycles on a G1 , and Boston Dynamics reports that a policy trained for 50 to 70 pound loads moved a fridge of over 100 pounds . Yutang Lin, Guanya Shi and C. Karen Liu at Amazon FAR, Carnegie Mellon and Stanford (October 2026) plan in the latent command space of a frozen behavior foundation model, which closes the balance loop at 50 Hz while their FIBER planner replans at 5 Hz . FIBER projects separately trained policies for box pickup, door opening and grasping into that space and trains one perceptive planner on their rollouts; across 128 simulated variations per task it succeeded 42.0% of the time, against 11.6% for replaying the projected latents, 3.5% for a kinematic planner and 95.4% for the task experts . Trained only in simulation, FIBER succeeded in 6, 4 and 2 of 10 real G1 trials on the three tasks . Zeji Yi, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Carnegie Mellon and Amazon FAR (October 2026) split collision avoidance between a perception-conditioned diffusion policy that proposes whole-body motions and an RL controller that tracks them and keeps balance . Their SWAP labels training data in hindsight, placing obstacles only where an executed motion did not sweep . Across five simulated tasks it averaged 88.3% success with test-time steering, 72.4% without it and 17.4% when the diffusion output drove the joints directly . On a real G1, with motion capture for localization and the moving obstacles, it succeeded in 18 of 25 trials; the authors trace the failures to LiDAR occlusion and tracking mismatch . HITTER pairs a planner that predicts the ball and picks the strike with an RL whole-body controller, and reached up to 106 consecutive table-tennis shots against a human . LATENT builds humanoid tennis skills by correcting and composing incomplete human motion fragments . Chris Paxton of Agility Robotics wrote in October 2026 that many such systems still see the ball through external motion trackers, which leaves onboard perception as the limit . Retargeting is lossy: artifacts such as foot sliding and self-penetration significantly reduce tracking-policy robustness, particularly for dynamic or long sequences , and noisy, inconsistent transferred references motivated a 2026 robustness method with a fall-recovery curriculum . Nicholas Ioannidis, Xue Bin Peng and colleagues at Simon Fraser University, FieldAI and NVIDIA (October 2026) replace the weighted objectives of retargeting with a priority order: foot placement first, then contacts with objects or other characters, then the remaining pose objectives . On two-person interactions from Inter-X their PriMoRetarget kept 78.8% of source hand contacts, and PPO policies trained on its output tracked the motions on a simulated Unitree G1 93.6% of the time . The strongest of three baselines, PHC, reached 35.2% and 72.8%; GMR and OmniRetarget scored lower . Collaborative manipulation by several robots stayed harder, at 62.6% tracking success . Chaitanya Chawla, Kartik Sharma, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Carnegie Mellon (October 2026) check reachability during generation: their EmbodyHOI steers a frozen generator of human hand-object motion with a differentiable inverse-kinematics cost for the target robot while it samples . On the Unitree G1 this cut the wrist error left after retargeting from 8.9 cm to 0.6 cm, and simulated policies trained on the guided references succeeded on 79% of 50 randomly drawn tasks, against 68% for unguided references . Fixing the arms with inverse kinematics after generation dropped success on a four-task suite to 32.8%, against 79.7% with guidance, which costs 32 times an unguided sample .
